subject: SOC2 / SIG evidence bucketization and portal onboarding for CloudTrek
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@cloudtrek.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: security@cloudtrek.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Onboarding to Whistic / SIG upload — CloudTrek profile

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the intro. We're starting a security review with one of your enterprise teams and need to get CloudTrek's SIG profile and evidence uploaded into Whistic. We have an exported SIG in PDF and a CSV manifest of controls, but our security ops want guidance on how Redwood prefers evidence to be organized ("bucketized") in the portal so the reviewers have a clean path through SOC 2 mappings.

Can you confirm:
- Preferred top-level buckets (e.g., SOC2, network, IAM, infra logs)?
- Any filename or metadata conventions Redwood expects?
- Who at Redwood will be the profile owner once uploaded?

I've attached the SIG export and a manifest. We can also provide individual artifacts if you want them grouped differently.

Elena
Elena Morales
Security Operations, CloudTrek
elena@cloudtrek.com
Attachments: cloudtrek_SIG-v2.pdf (PDF, 3.1 MB); evidence_manifest.csv (CSV, 22 KB)

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena@cloudtrek.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Onboarding to Whistic / SIG upload — CloudTrek profile

Hi Elena — thanks for sending these over. High level: we prefer evidence grouped by control family first (e.g., Logical Access / Change Mgmt / Monitoring), with SOC 2 mapping included in the manifest rows. A couple of practical preferences we use for easier review: 

- Top-level buckets: 01_SOC2_MAPPINGS, 02_IAM, 03_NETWORKING, 04_LOGS, 05_POLICIES_PROCEDURES, 06_THIRD_PARTY
- Filenames: <bucket>_<controlID>_<short-desc>_<YYYYMMDD>.<ext> (helps reviewers sort)
- Metadata we add in Whistic: control tags, evidence_date, retention_period, and contact.owner (email)

For ownership: once uploaded we ask that the vendor points to a single profile custodian; on Redwood's side we set a "portal owner" for the account who will be the escalation contact (I'll be the owner for initial intake, Mina will be the curator for SOC 2 mapping).

Next steps I suggest:
1) You upload the ZIP or individual files into Whistic under those buckets.
2) Send us the manifest with a new column named redwood_bucket that shows how you want each row mapped to our buckets.
3) We'll run a quick pass and return a short gap list (if anything is missing or needs redaction).

I'll put Mina on a follow-up to accept the manifest and start the mapping.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Manager, Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
To: Elena Morales <elena@cloudtrek.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 15:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Onboarding to Whistic / SIG upload — CloudTrek profile

Elena — quick note from Mina. Thanks for the files; I downloaded cloudtrek_SIG-v2.pdf and the manifest. Attached is a template CSV I use to translate vendor manifests into our bucket model (column names: vendor_control_id, vendor_filename, vendor_date, redwood_bucket, redwood_control_map, notes). Could you fill redwood_bucket for the rows you think belong in each bucket? If you prefer, we can do a short screen share where I map the first 30 rows and you confirm.

A few gotchas to watch for:
- Evidence that is time-series (e.g., 7 days of logs) should be represented as a single summary artifact + a pointer to the archive (don’t upload 7 separate large log files).
- For IAM evidence, include screenshots or exported role lists and separate out service accounts vs human users.
- If you redact IP addresses, add a redaction_explanation field.

I've created a temporary intake ticket: SEC-423 and uploaded the template to the linked drive. Once we have the mapped manifest, Marcus will run a lightweight validation and then I’ll request the portal import.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Security Intake Curator, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_mapping_template.csv (CSV, 5 KB)

From: Elena Morales <elena@cloudtrek.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: security@cloudtrek.com
Date: Wed, 17 Jan 2028 11:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Onboarding to Whistic / SIG upload — CloudTrek profile

Hi Grace / Mina — we completed the mapping and uploaded the initial set to Whistic under the buckets you suggested. Quick status: most items mapped cleanly, but we have two items that CloudTrek InfoSec wants to hold back (PCI-scoped screenshots with card hashes). I marked those rows in the manifest with redaction_explanation and placed the artifacts in a private S3 share referenced in the manifest (s3://cloudtrek-sec/priv-evidence/).

We also hit one validation note Marcus called out (missing retention metadata for several policy PDFs). I added retention_period and contact.owner for those rows and re-uploaded. Please let us know if you want the private artifacts sent to a secured upload link or if Redwood prefers we hand them to an SSO-enabled transfer.

Thanks for the clear template — the screen share would help for the last 12 rows if you’re available.

Best,
Elena

--
Elena Morales
Security Operations, CloudTrek
